easy.def: A group of friends.
examples: My posse and I played ball.
Her posse sat together.
He and his posse went to the park.

more.def: A group of friends who spend time together.
examples: She walked into class with her posse of best friends.
He and his posse of cousins played soccer all afternoon.
My posse of friends went to the park after school.

easy.def: To own or have.
examples: She possesses a rare coin.
I possess a key.
He possesses great strength.

more.def: To own or have something.
examples: The old castle possesses a hidden room.
The museum possesses a very old map.
The family possesses land by the river.

easy.def: Something that you own.
examples: This book is my possession.
He packed his possessions.
Her favorite possession is a doll.

more.def: Something that belongs to you.
examples: This bike is my favorite possession.
He packed all his possessions into a box.
The family lost most of its possessions in the flood.

easy.def: Showing who owns something.
examples: "My" is a possessive word.
"Mine" is possessive.
"Tom's" is possessive.

more.def: Showing who owns something, as "my" and "Tom's" do.
examples: "Her" is a possessive word in "her hat."
The possessive form of "dog" is "dog's."
We underlined each possessive word in the sentence.

easy.def: Something that may happen.
examples: There is a possibility of rain.
A snow day is a possibility.
Winning is a possibility.

more.def: A thing that might happen or might be true.
examples: There is a possibility that the game will be canceled.
Scientists studied the possibility of life on other planets.
We talked about every possibility before choosing a name.

easy.def: Able to happen.
examples: It is possible to fly.
Is it possible to go?
Rain is possible.

more.def: Able to happen, be done or be true.
examples: It is possible to see the stars from here on a clear night.
Is it possible to finish before lunch?
Snow is possible tomorrow, but it may rain instead.

easy.def: Maybe.
examples: It may possibly rain.
Could you possibly help?
He possibly forgot.

more.def: It could be, but it is not certain.
examples: It may possibly snow tonight.
Could you possibly lend me a pencil?
She is possibly the fastest runner in school.

easy.def: An animal that plays dead when it is scared.
examples: A possum hid in the tree.
The possum plays dead.
We saw a possum at night.

more.def: A small gray animal with a pointed face and a long tail that comes out at night and pretends to be dead when it is frightened.
examples: A possum crept across the yard at night looking for food.
When the possum is scared, it plays dead.
The possum carried her babies on her back.

easy.def: A tall piece of wood or metal in the ground.
examples: The fence post is tall.
A post holds the sign.
The horse is tied to the post.

more.def: A strong, upright piece of wood or metal set in the ground.
examples: Dad nailed the sign to a post.
The horse was tied to a fence post.
A tall post held up the porch roof.

easy.def: To put up a sign or message.
examples: Post the sign.
She posted a picture.
He posted a note.

more.def: To put up a notice or message where people can see it.
examples: The teacher posted the schedule on the door.
She posted a photo on the class page.
He posted a sign by the gate.

easy.def: To send a letter.
examples: Post the letter.
I posted a card.
He posts letters.

more.def: To send something by mail.
examples: Mom posted the letter on the way to work.
I posted a card to my cousin.
He posts packages on Fridays.

easy.def: The money you pay to mail something.
examples: The postage was a dollar.
I bought postage.
The letter needs postage.

more.def: The cost of mailing a letter or package, shown by a stamp.
examples: The postage for the package was five dollars.
A stamp shows that the postage has been paid.
The postage went up this year.

easy.def: Having to do with the mail.
examples: A postal worker came.
The postal service delivers mail.
A postal truck.

more.def: Having to do with the post office or the mail.
examples: A postal worker delivers letters to every house on our street.
The postal service sends packages across the country.
I need a postal stamp for this envelope.

easy.def: A card with a picture that you mail.
examples: I got a postcard.
The postcard has a beach.
She sent a postcard.

more.def: A card with a picture on one side that is sent through the mail without an envelope.
examples: I got a postcard from my aunt.
The postcard showed a beach.
She sent us a postcard from Paris.

easy.def: A big picture or sign on a wall.
examples: I hung a poster.
The poster is of a tiger.
The poster is on my wall.

more.def: A large printed picture or notice that is put on a wall.
examples: I hung a poster of a tiger on my wall.
A poster at school told about the fair.
The movie poster was bright and colorful.

easy.def: A person who brings the mail.
examples: The postman brought a card.
Our postman waves.
The postman came at noon.

more.def: A person whose job is to collect letters and packages and bring them to homes.
examples: The postman brought a package to our door.
Our postman walks down the street with a bag full of letters.
We wave to the postman every morning.

easy.def: To put off until later.
examples: We postponed the game.
The picnic was postponed.
They postponed the trip.

more.def: To move something to a later time.
examples: We postponed the game because of rain.
The picnic was postponed until Saturday.
They postponed the trip for a week.

easy.def: How you hold your body when you sit or stand.
examples: Stand with good posture.
Her posture is straight.
Good posture is healthy.

more.def: The way you hold your body when you sit, stand or walk.
examples: Sit up straight to have good posture.
The ballerina had perfect posture.
Slouching over a desk is bad for your posture.

easy.def: A deep round dish for cooking.
examples: Mom cooked soup in a big pot.
The pot is hot.
Put the pasta in the pot.

more.def: A deep, round container used for cooking or for holding plants.
examples: The soup simmered in a big pot on the stove.
She planted a seed in a small clay pot.
He stirred the pot of chili with a wooden spoon.

easy.def: A round vegetable that grows in the ground.
examples: I eat a baked potato.
Potatoes grow underground.
Mom mashed the potato.

more.def: A round vegetable with brown skin that grows under the ground.
examples: Dad baked a potato for dinner.
Potatoes grow underground, and farmers dig them up.
She made French fries from a potato.

easy.def: What someone could become.
examples: She has potential.
He has great potential as a swimmer.
The potential is there.

more.def: The ability to grow, develop or become something in the future.
examples: The coach saw great potential in the young player.
The seed has the potential to become a tall tree.
She has the potential to be a good writer.

easy.def: A hole in a road.
examples: The car hit a pothole.
A pothole is in the road.
There is a pothole.

more.def: A hole in the surface of a road, caused by wear and weather.
examples: The car bounced when it hit a pothole.
Workers filled the pothole with asphalt.
I rode around the pothole on my bike.

easy.def: A magic drink in a story.
examples: The witch made a potion.
The potion was green.
She drank the potion.

more.def: A liquid in stories that is said to have magic powers.
examples: The witch stirred a bubbling potion.
In the story, a potion made him invisible.
The wizard mixed a potion in a cauldron.

easy.def: Things made from baked clay, like pots and bowls.
examples: I made pottery in art class.
The pottery is red.
She sells pottery.

more.def: Pots, bowls and other things that are made from clay and baked until they are hard.
examples: I made a bowl in pottery class and painted it blue.
The museum has pottery from ancient Greece.
She sells handmade pottery at the market.

easy.def: A small bag, or a pocket on an animal's body.
examples: The kangaroo has a pouch.
I put coins in a pouch.
The baby is in the pouch.

more.def: A small bag, or a pocket of skin on an animal's body, such as the one on a kangaroo.
examples: The baby kangaroo rode in its mother's pouch.
He kept his coins in a leather pouch.
The pelican has a stretchy pouch under its beak.

easy.def: Birds raised on farms for eggs or meat.
examples: The farm has poultry.
Chickens are poultry.
We saw poultry at the fair.

more.def: Farm birds such as chickens, ducks and turkeys that are raised for eggs or meat.
examples: Chickens and ducks are kinds of poultry.
The farmer fed the poultry every morning.
We saw poultry at the county fair.

easy.def: To jump on something suddenly.
examples: The cat pounced.
The tiger pounces.
She pounced on the ball.

more.def: To jump suddenly and grab something or land on it.
examples: The cat crouched and pounced on the toy mouse.
The tiger pounced on its prey.
The puppy pounced on the ball.

easy.def: A way to measure how heavy something is.
examples: The baby weighs ten pounds.
I bought a pound of apples.
A pound of flour is heavy.

more.def: A unit for measuring weight, equal to 16 ounces.
examples: The baby weighed eight pounds.
We bought a pound of apples.
The bag of flour weighs five pounds.

easy.def: To hit again and again.
examples: Rain pounded on the roof.
He pounded the drum.
Waves pound the shore.

more.def: To hit something hard many times.
examples: Rain pounded on the roof all night.
He pounded the nail into the board.
Waves pound the shore during a storm.

easy.def: To make water flow out of something.
examples: Pour the milk into the cup.
I pour water on the plant.
She poured the juice.

more.def: To tip a container so that a liquid flows out.
examples: Dad poured the batter into the pan.
Rain began to pour down all at once.
He poured water from the pitcher into each glass.

easy.def: To push out your lips because you are upset.
examples: She pouted.
Do not pout.
He pouted at bedtime.

more.def: To push out your lips and look upset because you did not get what you wanted.
examples: She pouted when she had to go to bed early.
The little boy pouted because he could not have another cookie.
Don't pout; try to play a different game.

easy.def: Being very poor.
examples: Some families live in poverty.
Poverty means having little money.
People help to fight poverty.

more.def: The state of having very little money or not enough to live on.
examples: Many families in the town lived in poverty and needed help.
Volunteers worked to fight poverty by giving out food and clothing.
He grew up in poverty but worked hard to build a better life.

easy.def: Very tiny bits of something dry.
examples: The powder is soft.
I put powder on.
Flour is a powder.

more.def: A dry material made of very tiny pieces, like dust.
examples: Flour is a white powder.
The chalk crumbled into powder.
She put a spoonful of cocoa powder in the milk.

easy.def: Soft and fine like powder.
examples: The snow is powdery.
The sand was powdery.
She had powdery flour on her hands.

more.def: Like powder, or covered with fine, dry dust.
examples: The powdery snow flew up as we skied.
A powdery layer of flour covered the table.
The moth's wings left a powdery dust on my finger.

easy.def: The strength to make things happen.
examples: The wave had great power.
I used all my power to push.
Superheroes have special powers.

more.def: The ability or strength to do something or to make something happen.
examples: A hurricane has enough power to knock down trees.
Whales have great power in their tails.
The king had the power to make new laws.

easy.def: Energy that makes machines work.
examples: The storm cut the power to our street.
Solar panels make power from sunlight.
We lost power, so I used a flashlight.

more.def: Energy, especially electricity, that is used to run machines and light buildings.
examples: The power went out in the whole city during the storm.
Windmills turn wind into power for homes.
A small battery gives power to the toy car.

easy.def: Very strong.
examples: A powerful engine.
The wind was powerful.
He is a powerful swimmer.

more.def: Having great power or strength.
examples: The powerful engine lifted the rocket.
A powerful storm knocked down trees.
The king was a powerful ruler.

easy.def: Not able to do anything.
examples: I felt powerless.
The storm left us powerless.
The town was powerless.

more.def: Without strength, control or the ability to act.
examples: I felt powerless when I could not help my friend.
The little boat was powerless against the big waves.
They were powerless to stop the rain.
